..
Issued at 240 PM EDT Tue Oct 27 2026

Pattern Synopsis: Split flow pattern across North America...with the 
Great Lakes mainly under the influence of southern branch flow 
emanating around a mean trough across western North America.  Long 
wave ridge axis extends north from the Gulf...through the Midwest 
and into central Canada.  There is also an old upper low northeast 
of Hawaii that may have some impacts for the start of next week. 
Water vapor imagery shows several short wave troughs propagating 
through the western long wave trough...one lifting into northwest 
Ontario this afternoon with a second on its heels tracking into 
Iowa/Missouri.   Farther upstream additional pieces of energy across 
Montana/Wyoming and along the Oregon/ northern California coast. 
Elongated band of deeper moisture (precipitable water values around 
1.25 inches) extends north from the western Gulf into the upper 
Lakes...dynamic forcing with short wave troughs/right entrance 
region jet forcing interacting with this narrow moisture plume 
generating showers from western Upper/ Minnesota/western Wisconsin 
southward into Iowa/ eastern Kansas.  At the surface...1035mb high 
centered over northeast Ontario bringing east/southeast boundary 
layer flow into the region...though with veering winds quickly above 
the surface indicative of low level warm advection.  1018mb surface 
low over southwest Minnesota with a warm front extending southeast 
into the Ohio Valley...and a trailing cold front across Iowa/Kansas. 

Primary Forecast Concerns:

Small rain chances continue tonight...ending west to east: Not much 
out there at mid afternoon...better shower coverage just scraped by 
IWD before lifting north...and activity across Wisconsin is pretty 
spotty even with the best jet forcing in place (which will wane this 
evening).  Even with things drying out aloft overnight do have some 
concerns about lingering low level moisture and perhaps some drizzle 
developing across the western third of Upper Michigan overnight.

Warmer Wednesday with additional (much needed) rain chances Wednesday 
night: It will be warmer...to what magnitude is the question 
Consensus NBM forecast highs are really enthusiastic (lots of upper 
60s and lower 70s). There is still a lot of cloud cover out there 
and concerned that especially over western Upper this could tamp 
temperatures down. Have added in some raw temperature guidance 
to the NBM to tone things down a touch...still have highs in the
lower to mid 60s which is pretty good considering our normal 
highs now in the mid to upper 40s. Think the eastern half of 
Upper Michigan stands the best chance for seeing some more sun 
Wednesday. Better rain chances in the cards by late Wednesday 
afternoon/night ahead of an approaching cold front and a narrow 
low level theta-e ridge axis. Anticipating a band of showers and
some embedded thunderstorms with instability within the theta-e
ridge. Should be a quick hitter as rain threat expected to be 
east of the forecast area by mid-Thursday morning. Overall 
rainfall amounts generally 0.25 or less on average...but better 
than nothing. 

Dry and turning cooler Thursday: Cold front will sweep across the 
Upper Peninsula by Thursday morning...with winds shifting to the 
west and northwest as cooler air invades from the northwest.  High 
temperatures may be earlier in the day Thursday and may see 
temperatures cool during the afternoon.  Should be a bit breezy as 
well...with winds diminishing Thursday night as high pressure builds 
into the Great Lakes from the west. 

Unsettled to start next week? Uncertainty abounds: Earlier mentioned 
upper low northeast of Hawaii may make an appearance over the 
central/southern Plains this weekend...at least what remains of it 
by then.  Whether we see any rainy impacts from this feature during 
the latter half of the weekend and into Monday is uncertain.  There 
will be low chance PoPs in the forecast for some areas Sunday and 
Monday given the possibility that we could see some rain push into 
Upper Michigan to end the weekend...though right now the probability 
appears to be small.  The high that builds into the Great Lakes 
Friday is forecast to move into New England by Saturday...a return 
to more southerly winds should keep temperatures above normal 
through the weekend...keeping the very warm October theme intact 
until the very end.
